previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of end-stage renal disease due to diabetic nephropathy, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for chest pain in the setting of hypertensive urgency with systolic blood pressures up to 240 mmHg. He presented with substernal pressure radiating to the back and evidence of mild to moderate pulmonary edema on chest imaging. His troponin was minimally elevated but consistent with his baseline due to chronic kidney disease. He was treated with intravenous nitroglycerin to control blood pressure and IV furosemide for fluid overload, with improvement in symptoms and resolution of pulmonary congestion. A renal ultrasound ruled out renal artery stenosis, and transplant nephrology recommended outpatient evaluation for pheochromocytoma. His antihypertensive regimen was optimized with increased labetalol and discontinuation of nifedipine. He was discharged home on adjusted medications, with instructions to monitor weight and blood pressure, and to follow up for a sleep study, chem 7, and pheochromocytoma workup.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure

69%), ESRD due to diabetic nephropathy s/p failed renal 
transplant in ___ and S/P repeat renal transplant in ___ with 
stage 4 CKD (baseline Cr recently 3.8-4), calciphylaxis, OSA 
(used O2 3 LPM at night), PAD s/p multiple bilateral 
revascularizations and left BKA presenting with dyspnea and 
hypertension.

Mr. ___ noticed on ___ afternoon that his home SBPs were in 
the 240s all day while he was checking it. He said that he 
usually checks his blood pressure 3 times a day with an 
automated arm blood pressure cuff. He says that he has been very 
compliant with his home antihypertensive medications. However, 
upon discussing the doses with him, he realizes that he may have 
been taking only 1 of the labetalol tablets as opposed to the 
usual two that he had been taking. He states that he got a 
recent prescription that was 200 mg as opposed to the previous 
300 mg tablets and therefore he was possibly taking only two 
tablets in the AM and evening as opposed to the 3 that he should 
be taking to make the total 600 mg dose AM and QHS. 

On ___ evening after his BP was elevated all day, he had 
wheeziness with his breathing and a tightness and pressure in 
his chest. He says that this has happened before and was similar 
each time. He had taken his medications. He also had some cough, 
with clear mucus, but no fevers or chills (T 98.2F). He did take 
his medications. He has been admitted multiple times previously 
for similar presentations due to poorly controlled hypertension.

He was admitted from ___ through ___ for 
hypertensive urgency with atypical chest pain. At that time, his 
systolic blood pressure ranged between 170-240, and this was 
similarly associated with this chest tightness. His chest 
discomfort was thought to be secondary to subendocardial 
ischemia from strain with the elevated afterload. His baseline 
troponins are thought do be around 0.18 given his ESRD. On that 
hospitalization, he required a nitroglycerin drip before being 
able to be controlled on his home blood pressure regimen. 
Notably a renal ultrasound was negative for evidence of renal 
artery stenosis on admission. There was a recommendation to do a 
pheochromocytoma work-up as an outpatient. He also required 
diuresis with furosemide IV before being placed back in his home 
regimen.

In the ED, initial vital signs were notable for: Temp 98.6 HR 72 
BP 244/109 RR 18 SaO2 96% on O2 2 LPM via NC. Exam notable for a 
right-sided port, regular rhythm, left-sided crackles, left BKA, 
no peripheral edema. Labs were notable for WBC 6.6 Hgb 8.5 Plt 
134 INR: 1.2 Na 141 K 3.4 Cl 100 HC03 23 BUN 71 Cr. 4.7 Trop-T 
0.17 -> 0.20 -> 0.18, NT-Pro-BNP: 34718. UA: protein 300, Ketone 
neg, Bacteria few. Renal US showed abnormal intrarenal waveforms 
demonstrating absence of antegrade diastolic flow corresponding 
with a resistive index of 1.0. Patient was given nitroglycerin 
0.3 mg sl X 2, pravastatin 40 mg, labetolol 600+400+600 mg po, 
nifedpine 90 mg po, furosemide 60 mg IV, tacrolimus 0.5+4.5 mg, 
prednisone 3 mg, insulin 2+2+4 units, Creon 12 3 cap. Renal felt 
there was no urgent indication for hemodialysis and advised 
re-dosing furosemide to maintain urine output of 100-125 cc/hr 
with goal negative 2 L over 24 hours. They also recommended 
titrating down TNG infusion to slowly reduce BP but not less 
than SBP of 160 on the day of admission. Vital signs on 
transfer: Temp 98.3 HR 71 BP 168/71 RR 18 O2 sat 98% on RA.

After arrival to the cardiology ward, the patient confirmed the 
above history. He said that overall his breathing was much 
improved and he was not as wheezy. He stated that he continued 
to have the chest discomfort located at the xiphoid area of his 
abdomen/chest. He did not feel that it radiated into his arms or 
spreads to his back. He said that overall it was much more 
tolerable and he also thought that there may be a component of 
gastritis to his chest tightness. Interestingly he described 
this as if there is a baseball or something taking up space in 
the epigastric/xiphoid area.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: He denied any dysuria, hematuria, fevers, 
chills, lower extremity edema, weight gain, nausea, vomiting, 
diarrhea. The remainder of a complete ROS was negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ man with a history of ESRD secondary 
to diabetic nephropathy (s/p failed Left RRRT in ___ and now 
S/P DDRT in ___ with stage 4 
transplant CKD), calciphylaxis and subsequent left BKA, PAD S/P 
multiple bilateral revascularizations, HFpEF (LVEEF 69%), OSA, 
who presented with hypertensive urgency and chest pain. 
Patient's blood pressure was very difficult to control but he 
was discharged on a stable regimen.

ACTIVE ISSUES: 
# Severe asymptomatic hypertension, chest pain: Patient with 
acute onset shortness of breath, wheezing and variable 
descriptions of chest tightness in setting of severe 
hypertension with SBP in 240s. This likely led to a pulmonary 
hypertensive state and increased wall stretch and stress leading 
to possible subendocardial ischemia. Troponin-T elevated but at 
baseline in setting of ESRD. There was no rise and fall in 
troponin-T to suggest an acute myonecrotic event. Etiology of 
his recurrent hypertensive episodes and frequent 
hospitalizations remains unclear. Urine metanepherines were low. 
Transplant renal ultrasound was without obvious inflow artery 
stenosis. Labile blood pressures intermittently requiring 
nitroglycerin drip as well as midodrine because he became 
symptomatic with occasional systolic blood pressure <130 mmHg. 
Nifedipine was discontinued and he was discharged on amlodipine 
10 mg, doxazosin 16 mg, labetalol 800 mg TID, and hydralazine 
100 mg PO TID.

# Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting: Patient with severe, 
acute-onset epigastric pain with benign abdominal exam. Given 
vascular history, initial thoughts that this was hypo-perfusion 
related mesenteric infarct in setting of relative hypotension. 
Lactate and abdominal X ray were normal without obstructive 
pattern. This resolved prior to discharge with better blood 
pressure control. 

# Pulmonary edema, HFpEF: Patient with heart failure preserved 
ejection fraction and acute onset pulmonary edema in the setting 
of hypertensive urgency. Overall on exam he appeared to be 
euvolemic and his weight per the report from home and from his 
vitals did not suggest a volume overloaded state. He received 
furosemide IV in the ED but he was transitioned to his home 
torsemide shortly after admission. Heart failure therapy was 
directed at better control of his systolic blood pressure.

# Thrombocytopenia (RESOLVED): Patient with acute onset from 
thrombocytopenia with platelets in the 130s from previous 
170-190 baseline. His platelets were monitored and normalized 
prior to discharge. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Diabetes mellitus, type 2: Last A1C 6.4 % on ___. He was 
continued on a reduced dose of his home glargine 13 units a.m at 
8 units.

# Peripheral arterial disease: Patient with prior left leg 
dorsalis pedis bypass with resultant left below the knee 
amputation setting of infection. He uses a prosthetic leg. He 
was continued on aspirin 81 mg PO daily and his pravastatin was 
changed to atorvastatin 40 mg PO qhs.

# ESRD s/p ___ renal transplant ___: ESRD secondary to diabetic 
nephropathy (s/p failed LRRT in ___ now with a functioning DDRT 
implanted in ___. Baseline Cr ___. He continued daily 
prednisone 3 mg daily as well as tacrolimus increased to 5 mg 
BID. He will follow-up with transplant nephrology as outpatient. 
He does not need to continue taking his leflunomide.

# Pancreatic insufficiency: Patient has a history of chronic 
epigastric pain and a history of pancreatic insufficiency. He 
was continued on his home Creon 3 times daily with meals

# Chronic anemia: Patient with baseline anemia hemoglobin 
baseline between 7.9-8.5.
Normocytic and likely related to CKD.

# OSA: Patient was unable to use CPAP machine as an outpatient 
and requires repeat sleep study. Baseline use of O2 3 LPM via NC 
at night.

# Right native kidney mass: MRI ___ showed small complex 
renal cysts. Will repeat US in ___ year.
